result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers praise the form's structure and reject wizards and floating labels. Both also frame the emergency notice as a major fix rather than optional polish. B stays closer to the markup: it covers the Species default, the 'Other' option and the 'within one working day' line, and it keeps its severity labels in proportion. A adds more speculative problems (spam protection, new or existing client, preferred contact method, fieldsets) and makes a vague 'usability research' claim. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the form's structure is sound and both warn against wizards and floating labels. A ties every point closely to the markup and sticks to issues that are actually there, though it frames them as 'Fix first' with severity labels rather than as optional polish. B lists eight 'real problems', several of them speculative (spam protection, new-client field, fieldsets). It also cites unsupported usability research and recommends cosmetic changes such as photos, cards and placeholders, so it is weaker on restraint and on avoiding invented facts.
